axes.model_access:
The official Available Models page lists the full roster: the Anthropic Claude family (Fable 5.1/5, Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5/5, Haiku 4.5),
Google Gemini (3.8/3.7 Flash, 3.1 Pro), OpenAI GPT (6.1 Sol, 6 Astra, 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, 5.5),
xAI Grok 4.6/4.5, Zhipu GLM 5.3 Flash/5.2 and Moonshot Kimi K3/K2.7 Code (hosted on Fireworks/Baseten),
plus in-house Prism (a model ensemble combining Claude and GPT; the Prism option routes across curated model families).
Billing is token-based (Token-Based Pricing page: three segments — LLM tokens + Cosmos compute + service fee).
axes.runtime:
The main line is the Cosmos platform (official Introduction: five building blocks — Environments/Experts/Sessions/Capabilities/Triggers):
it chains plan-implement-review-feedback into a repeatable Software Factory workflow (four official loops:
Requirements→Ticket, Ticket→PR, PR→Merge, Signal→Ticket). Environments come in three flavors: Augment-hosted cloud sandbox, your own VM/physical machine
(self-hosted daemon), or even your local laptop. There is also the Auggie CLI (terminal agent: repo implementation / code exploration / running tests / CI automation)
and IDE extension surfaces for VS Code / JetBrains.
axes.local_files:
IDE extensions and the Auggie CLI work on local codebases; Cosmos's Environments decide where the code lives — hosted cloud sandbox,
self-hosted daemon (running on your own infrastructure, configured via daemon-config.json for workspace and isolation) or local.
The self-hosted surface is an official first-class citizen (the official page explicitly says own virtual or physical infrastructure).
axes.background:
Cosmos leads with long-horizon multi-step delivery: durable environments, scheduled automations,
cross-repo cross-tool coordination (wording from the official llms.txt usage guide); Triggers wire events into the loop.
The official narrative is an "always-on software delivery system" — running continuously from spec to verification.
axes.fit:
Good fit: the enterprise "software factory" narrative — agent pipelines across the SDLC (ticket→PR→merge→monitor),
self-hosted environments running agents on your own infrastructure, one of the fullest frontier-model rosters (with in-house Prism routing).
Not a fit: looking for a personal free tier to get started (the main line is enterprise delivery with token billing);
readers who need product ownership to be stable — since 2026-10 the Cosmos/Auggie CLI/Context Engine assets have been joining Harness.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement** (three, each pointing at something the official readable pages do not give):

- **Actual changes to the purchase/renewal path after the Harness integration** (the announcement only covers assets and team joining; no customer migration details)
- **Isolation and audit behavior of the self-hosted daemon in real CI** (there is an official daemon-config page; not measured)
- **Actual transparency of Prism routing's model choice** (can you see which model each request lands on)
unknowns:
- Brand and product-line direction after the Harness integration (the official announcement gives no complete statement)
- Whether personal/small-team plans exist (navigation is enterprise-sales-led; no personal tier verified)
- Code storage region and retention policy of the hosted cloud sandbox (not verified item by item)
- Details of the individual-side permission model (not verified item by item)
related: Same "async delivery agent" narrative: Devin leads with a cloud autonomous engineer; Augment leads with enterprise SDLC pipelines and self-hosted.
Both multi-model coding platforms: Cursor centers on the editor; Augment centers on the Cosmos pipeline and the Context Engine.
Terminal-agent counterpart: Auggie CLI and Claude Code both enter CI/CD — worth contrasting their context engines.
